contrary_evidence: AWS: ‘broadly exploited in the wild’ (attempts)
impact_on_conclusion: supports ‘attempts, no confirmed breaches’
notes: site confidence: reported

claim: watchTowr (Jake Knott): broad exploitation attempts, but the exploits being sprayed either don't work, test for timing-based differences, or crash the target.
impact_on_conclusion: supports ‘attempts, no confirmed RCE from circulating exploits’
notes: Consistent with Defused (21 Oct 18:10 UTC): https://x.com/DefusedCyber/status/2112969691668869611; site confidence: reported

claim: Precautionary takedowns in Germany (Charité fully offline, parts of berlin.de, Berlin police online station, FU Berlin IT; sites in Bavaria/Lower Saxony); per Reuters government sites offline in DK/FI/FR/NL; no reports of successful attacks at time of writing; packages from Debian, Fedora, Gentoo, Ubuntu, Red Hat, Slackware, SUSE.
primary_source_locus: heise (Dirk Knop), sections ‘Viele Webseiten offline’, ‘Massive Exploit-Versuche’, ‘Aktualisierte PHP-Installationspakete’
impact_on_conclusion: extends the shutdown wave to Germany; no-breach status
notes: heise cites dpa and Reuters; not organisation statements; site confidence: reported

claim: Censys: of 2.58M internet-facing hosts seen on 21 Oct, ~1.58M reported identifiable PHP versions and ~1.57M were not patched; ~3M PHP hosts tracked on 22 Oct.
contrary_evidence: Version-banner based; distro backports may not change the version string. Censys researcher Silas Cutler earlier estimated >1.3M (https://bsky.app/profile/silascutler.bsky.social/post/3mydwzp3dcc2z)
impact_on_conclusion: order of magnitude of unpatched exposure
notes: site confidence: estimate (scan-based estimate)

claim: Unit 42 (Palo Alto Networks): more than 22.6 million internet-exposed instances potentially vulnerable.
contrary_evidence: Counts instances, not hosts; not directly comparable with Censys/Modat
impact_on_conclusion: upper-bound style exposure estimate
notes: site confidence: estimate (scan-based estimate)

claim: PHP published minimal source backports for 7.4/8.0/8.1 (no releases); vendors shipped fixed EOL packages on 21 Oct: Ubuntu USN-8948-1 (php8.1, 22.04 LTS), Freexian ELTS (php7.0/7.3/7.4: ELA-1855-1/1854-1/1853-1), deb.sury.org (php8.1 8.1.34-9, 8.0, 7.4, 5.6).
primary_source_locus: php.net advisory ‘How to update’; https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8948-1; https://deb.freexian.com/extended-lts/tracker/CVE-2026-109618; https://packages.sury.org/php/ pool (build date 20261021)
impact_on_conclusion: EOL installations without such a vendor remain exposed
notes: see corr-010

claim: CISA KEV still has no entry for CVE-2026-109618/109619 (catalog 2026.10.21, checked 22 Oct 10:27 UTC).
contrary_evidence: AWS calls it ‘broadly exploited’ (attempts)
impact_on_conclusion: exploitation threshold for ‘confirmed’ not met

claim: Denmark: Copenhagen Municipality, Danish Road Directorate, DMI sites and the school platform Aula (Kombit) taken offline; minister Lisbeth Bech-Nielsen called it a ‘global incident’ but not a cyberattack.
impact_on_conclusion: adds Denmark to the precautionary shutdown wave
notes: site confidence: reported

claim: CrowdStrike says it verified end-to-end in the lab that a single anonymous POST request can make an Apache mod_php worker launch a shell and execute a command (no authentication, no vulnerable application code); per CrowdStrike, PHP's shipped defaults (post_max_size 8M, memory_limit 128M) are not reachable via the demonstrated path, exposure requires roughly memory_limit < 4 x post_max_size, and the only server-side trace is a memory-exhaustion fatal error 'in Unknown on line 0'.
primary_source_locus: CrowdStrike blog (Amit Serper), intro paragraph after the CVE list; 'Am I Impacted?'; CVE-2026-109618 section (log line)
contrary_evidence: watchTowr: circulating public exploits do not achieve RCE (SecurityWeek); Red Hat RHSB-2026-013 rates RCE 'difficult in practice' for PHP-FPM (https://access.redhat.com/security/vulnerabilities/RHSB-2026-013)
impact_on_conclusion: first major-vendor statement of a working RCE; narrows realistic exposure to mod_php and certain limit configurations; does not change 'no confirmed breaches'
notes: Vendor lab claim, not independently reproduced in public; exploit not published; ledger status mapped from site confidence "reported" to "unverified" (ledger vocabulary), 22 Oct 18:50 UTC

claim: X post counts (X API v2 recent counts, reposts included): 'php2shell' 263 (20 Oct), 27,345 (21 Oct), 27,913 (22 Oct to ~18:30 UTC); '#PHP2Shell' 4 / 2,971 / 6,811; CVE IDs 267 / 13,567 / 9,189.
impact_on_conclusion: measures attention, not risk; 22 Oct partial
notes: API counts as retrieved; site confidence: estimate (counts include reposts, partial day)

claim: About 40% of 'php2shell' posts on X were in Japanese (21,919 of 55,521, 20–22 Oct); German-language 1,431; Polish-language 352.
primary_source_locus: X API v2 counts with lang: operator
contrary_evidence: lang: is X's automatic language detection
impact_on_conclusion: Japan is the largest audience; link to the PM's appeal is analysis [A]
notes: site confidence: estimate

claim: infosec.exchange hashtag history for #php2shell: 508 uses by 372 accounts on 21 Oct; 234 uses by 188 accounts on 22 Oct (to ~18:30 UTC).
contrary_evidence: covers only posts federated to infosec.exchange
impact_on_conclusion: Mastodon attention lower than X
notes: site confidence: estimate

claim: The most discussed Hacker News story is 'There isn't an easy exploit for this PHP vulnerability' (597 points, 392 comments at retrieval); commenters report GitHub PoCs that need a pre-existing LFI or do not run.
contrary_evidence: tptacek (HN 50198093) and CrowdStrike: working RCE exists in research conditions
impact_on_conclusion: dominant mood = PoC skepticism
notes: observation (qualitative social-media reading by the editors); not a fact about the incident; site confidence: reported

claim: Polish- and German-language X is dominated by alarm / 'patch now' posts (e.g. @prywatnik 21 Oct 11:44 UTC, @Wilehalm 21 Oct 07:43 UTC).
contrary_evidence: hosting providers' status posts are calmer (@netcup)
impact_on_conclusion: describes tone, not events
notes: observation (qualitative social-media reading by the editors); not a fact about the incident; site confidence: reported

claim: Recurring moods besides skepticism and alarm: humour/Log4j comparisons, embargo/process criticism, EOL frustration, scam/backdoored-PoC warnings and memecoin spam, and (Poland) political jabs over the BIP shutdown.
primary_source_locus: HN 'Tell HN: I unknowingly broke the PHP RCE embargo' + X posts listed in §7.5
impact_on_conclusion: context for the reception chapter
notes: observation (qualitative social-media reading by the editors); not a fact about the incident; site confidence: reported

claim: Linux-Magazin frames the PHP Foundation's statement (OOM problem known since the 2024 Quarkslab audit, fix stalled) as a 'governance debacle'.
impact_on_conclusion: press framing of a fact already in §3.3
notes: time = editors' Mastodon post

claim: Contradiction: CrowdStrike reports lab-verified RCE on mod_php, while watchTowr (via Dark Reading) and heise's Christopher Kunz (via ZDFheute) say circulating exploits fail; IBM's Patrick Fussell (CNN) says it is not push-button.
contrary_evidence: https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/crowdstrike-protects-customers-from-php-rce-zero-days/
impact_on_conclusion: both can be true (lab RCE vs failing public scripts)

claim: '70% of the internet' (CNN, Onet) is PHP's share of websites with a known server-side language, not a count of vulnerable servers; CNBC notes not every PHP site is necessarily vulnerable.
contrary_evidence: CNN headline 'affecting 70% of the internet'
impact_on_conclusion: prevents over-reading the reach figure

claim: 'The attacks have begun' (SPIEGEL headline, 22 Oct 11:45 UTC) versus no confirmed successful compromise (Recorded Future; watchTowr via Dark Reading) and no CISA KEV entry.
contrary_evidence: https://www.recordedfuture.com/blog/php2shell-vulnerability-exploitation
impact_on_conclusion: attempts ≠ successful breaches

claim: On 23 Oct 2026 the PHP team published an informational advisory recommending session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular release; CVE-2026-115560 (possible RCE) needs session.serialize_handler set to php_binary/php_serialize and switched to php at runtime via ini_set() before session_start(), with upload progress enabled; not fixed by the 21 Oct releases.
primary_source_locus: news entry 'Informational advisory: Session upload progress' (23 Oct 2026)
impact_on_conclusion: the 21 Oct patches are not the last word; mitigation already advised on 21 Oct
notes: also BleepingComputer 23 Oct 15:38 UTC

claim: Sophos stopped an attempt to install Potassium (Mirai variant) via PHP2Shell and corrected an earlier report of successful exploitation; Arctic Wolf links Potassium binaries to PHP2Shell payload servers; Hunt.io attributes traffic to a Mirai-style botnet active since May 2026.
primary_source_locus: section 'Mirai botnet linked to exploitation attempts'
contrary_evidence: Arctic Wolf: no evidence the requests fetched or ran the malware
impact_on_conclusion: botnet operators are trying; no success shown
notes: second source: The Record (Arctic Wolf, Cobalt)

claim: VulnCheck says its (customer-only) exploit for CVE-2026-109618 reaches RCE on x86-64 with ASLR enabled and display_errors off, and knows of no other public or commercial exploit that does so.
contrary_evidence: Sophos/Sansec/watchTowr: public exploits fail on default production setups
impact_on_conclusion: ASLR is a hurdle, not a permanent barrier
notes: vendor claim; also SecurityWeek 23 Oct

claim: As of 23 Oct no successful in-the-wild compromise via PHP2Shell has been confirmed (SecurityWeek; The Record; Dataminr via BleepingComputer); Google's Hultquist: no validated exploitation, may have begun in a limited fashion.
contrary_evidence: AWS 'broadly exploited' wording (attempts); Sophos' retracted report
impact_on_conclusion: exploitation status stays 'attempts, no confirmed compromise'
notes: absence of reports, not proof of absence

claim: heise (citing Censys): over 41 million PHP services with vulnerable version numbers since Wednesday, about 8 million updated, 33.5 million left; Germany about 11 million services, about 4.2 million vulnerable; ~54% hide their version.
contrary_evidence: Censys via SecurityWeek 22 Oct: ~1.57 million unpatched hosts; Unit 42: 22.6 million instances (different units)
impact_on_conclusion: scale figures are estimates in different units
notes: site confidence: estimate

claim: X post counts (X API v2 recent counts, reposts included): 'php2shell' 32,333 on 22 Oct (peak) and 11,537 on 23 Oct to 18:20 UTC; '#PHP2Shell' 7,773 then 1,603; 'CVE-2026-115560' 1,385 on 23 Oct; infosec.exchange #php2shell 508/276/119 uses (21/22/23 Oct).
primary_source_locus: X API v2 GET /2/tweets/counts/recent, granularity=day; Mastodon hashtag history
impact_on_conclusion: measures attention, not risk; 23 Oct partial
notes: API counts as retrieved; site confidence: estimate

claim: After PHP's 23 Oct advisory, 'BREAKING/ANOTHER UNPATCHED' posts (e.g. @TheHackersNews, @coinbureau) dominate X, while practitioners' replies stress the rare configuration (e.g. @BreachByteSec, @AzmyBlog).
impact_on_conclusion: describes tone, not events
